chapters.name: Arjuna Visada Yoga
chapters.summary:
The first chapter of the Bhagavad Gita - "Arjuna Vishada Yoga" introduces the setup, the setting, the characters and the circumstances that led to the epic battle of Mahabharata, fought between the Pandavas and the Kauravas. It outlines the reasons that led to the revelation of the of Bhagavad Gita.
As both armies stand ready for the battle, the mighty warrior Arjuna, on observing the warriors on both sides becomes increasingly sad and depressed due to the fear of losing his relatives and friends and the consequent sins attributed to killing his own relatives. So, he surrenders to Lord Krishna, seeking a solution. Thus, follows the wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita.

chapters.name: Sankhya Yoga
chapters.summary:
The second chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sankhya Yoga". This is the most important chapter of the Bhagavad Gita as Lord Krishna condenses the teachings of the entire Gita in this chapter. This chapter is the essence of the entire Gita. 
"Sankhya Yoga" can be categorized into 4 main topics - 
1. Arjuna completely surrenders himself to Lord Krishna and accepts his position as a disciple and Krishna as his Guru. He requests Krishna to guide him on how to dismiss his sorrow.
2. Explanation of the main cause of all grief, which is ignorance of the true nature of Self.
3. Karma Yoga - the discipline of selfless action without being attached to its fruits.
4. Description of a Perfect Man - One whose mind is steady and one-pointed.

chapters.name: Karma Yoga
chapters.summary: The third chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Karma Yoga" or the "Path of Selfless Service". Here Lord Krishna emphasizes the importance of karma in life. He reveals that it is important for every human being to engage in some sort of activity in this material world. Further, he describes the kinds of actions that lead to bondage and the kinds that lead to liberation. Those persons who continue to perform their respective duties externally for the pleasure of the Supreme, without attachment to its rewards get liberation at the end.

chapters.name: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
chapters.meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
chapters.summary: The fourth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna glorifies the Karma Yoga and imparts the Transcendental Knowledge (the knowledge of the soul and the Ultimate Truth) to Arjuna. He reveals the reason behind his appearance in this material world. He reveals that even though he is eternal, he reincarnates time after time to re-establish dharma and peace on this Earth. His births and activities are eternal and are never contaminated by material flaws. Those persons who know and understand this Truth engage in his devotion with full faith and eventually attain Him. They do not have to take birth in this world again.

chapters.name: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
chapters.summary: The fifth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Karma Sanyasa Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna compares the paths of renunciation in actions (Karma Sanyas) and actions with detachment (Karma Yoga) and explains that both are means to reach the same goal and we can choose either. A wise person should perform his/her worldly duties without attachment to the fruits of his/her actions and dedicate them to God. This way they remain unaffected by sin and eventually attain liberation.

chapters.name: Dhyana Yoga
chapters.summary: The sixth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Dhyana Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the "Yoga of Meditation" and how to practise this Yoga. He discusses the role of action in preparing for Meditation, how performing duties in devotion purifies one's mind and heightens one's spiritual consciousness. He explains in detail the obstacles that one faces when trying to control their mind and the exact methods by which one can conquer their mind. He reveals how one can focus their mind on Paramatma and unite with the God.

chapters.name: Gyaan Vigyana Yoga
chapters.summary: The seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gyaan Vigyana Yoga ". In this chapter, Krishna reveals that he is the Supreme Truth, the principal cause and the sustaining force of everything. He reveals his illusionary energy in this material world called Maya, which is very difficult to overcome but those who surrender their minds unto Him attain Him easily. He also describes the four types of people who surrender to Him in devotion and the four kinds that don't. Krishna confirms that He is the Ultimate Reality and those who realize this Truth reach the pinnacle of spiritual realization and unite with the Lord.

chapters.name: Akshara Brahma Yoga
chapters.summary: The eighth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Akshara Brahma Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the importance of the last thought before death. If we can remember Krishna at the time of death, we will certainly attain him. Thus, it is very important to be in constant awareness of the Lord at all times, thinking of Him and chanting His names at all times. By perfectly absorbing their mind in Him through constant devotion, one can go beyond this material existence to Lord's Supreme abode.

chapters.name: Raja Vidya Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through the King of Sciences
chapters.summary: The ninth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Raja Vidya Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna explains that He is Supreme and how this material existence is created, maintained and destroyed by His Yogmaya and all beings come and go under his supervision. He reveals the Role and the Importance of Bhakti (transcendental devotional service) towards our Spiritual Awakening. In such devotion, one must live for the God, offer everything that he possesses to Him and do everything for Him only. One who follows such devotion becomes free from the bonds of this material world and unites with the Lord.

chapters.name: Vibhooti Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God
chapters.summary: The tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vibhooti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals Himself as the cause of all causes. He describes His various manifestations and opulences in order to increase Arjuna's Bhakti. Arjuna is fully convinced of Lord's paramount position and proclaims him to be the Supreme Personality. He prays to Krishna to describe more of His divine glories which are like nectar to hear.

chapters.name: Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God
chapters.summary: The eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga". In this chapter, Arjuna requests Krishna to reveal His Universal Cosmic Form that encompasses all the universes, the entire existence. Arjuna is granted divine vision to be able to see the entirety of creation in the body of the Supreme Lord Krishna.

chapters.name: Bhakti Yoga
chapters.summary: The twelfth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Bhakti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna emphasizes the superiority of Bhakti Yoga (the path of devotion) over all other types of spiritual disciplines and reveals various aspects of devotion. He further explains that the devotees who perform pure devotional service to Him, with their consciousness, merged in Him and all their actions dedicated to Him, are quickly liberated from the cycle of life and death. He also describes the various qualities of the devotees who are very dear to Him.

chapters.name: Ksetra Ksetrajna Vibhaaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field
chapters.summary: The thirteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Ksetra Ksetrajna Vibhaaga Yoga". The word "kshetra" means "the field", and the "kshetrajna" means "the knower of the field". We can think of our material body as the field and our immortal soul as the knower of the field. In this chapter, Krishna discriminates between the physical body and the immortal soul. He explains that the physical body is temporary and perishable whereas the soul is permanent and eternal. The physical body can be destroyed but the soul can never be destroyed. The chapter then describes God, who is the Supreme Soul. All the individual souls have originated from the Supreme Soul. One who clearly understands the difference between the body, the Soul and the Supreme Soul attains the realization of Brahman.

chapters.name: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
chapters.summary: The fourteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the three gunas (modes) of the material nature - goodness, passion and ignorance which everything in the material existence is influenced by. He further explains the essential characteristics of each of these modes, their cause and how they influence a living entity affected by them. He then reveals the various characteristics of the persons who have gone beyond these gunas. The chapter ends with Krishna reminding us of the power of pure devotion to God and how attachment to God can help us transcend these gunas.

chapters.name: Purushottama Yoga
chapters.meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
chapters.summary: The fifteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Purushottama Yoga". In Sanskrit, Purusha means the "All-pervading God", and Purushottam means the timeless & transcendental aspect of God.        Krishna reveals that the purpose of this Transcendental knowledge of the God is to detach ourselves from the bondage of the material world and to understand Krishna as the Supreme Divine Personality, who is the eternal controller and sustainer of the world. One who understands this Ultimate Truth surrenders to Him and engages in His devotional service.

chapters.name: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
chapters.summary: The sixteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes explicitly the two kinds of natures among human beings - divine and demoniac. Those who possess demonaic qualities associate themselves with the modes of passion and ignorance do not follow the regulations of the scriptures and embrace materialistic views. These people attain lower births and further material bondage. But people who possess divine qualities, follow the instructions of the scriptures, associate themselves with the mode of goodness and purify the mind through spiritual practices. This leads to the enhancement of divine qualities and they eventually attain spiritual realization.

chapters.name: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
chapters.summary: The seventeenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes the three types of faith corresponding to the three modes of the material nature. Lord Krishna further reveals that it is the nature of faith that determines the quality of life and the character of living entities. Those who have faith in passion and ignorance perform actions that yield temporary, material results while those who have faith in goodness perform actions in accordance with scriptural instructions and hence their hearts get further purified.

chapters.name: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
chapters.meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
chapters.summary: The eighteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Moksha Sanyas Yoga". Arjuna requests the Lord to explain the difference between the two types of renunciations - sanyaas(renunciation of actions) and tyaag(renunciation of desires). Krishna explains that a sanyaasi is one who abandons family and society in order to practise spiritual discipline whereas a tyaagi is one who performs their duties without attachment to the rewards of their actions and dedicating them to the God. Krishna recommends the second kind of renunciation - tyaag. Krishna then gives a detailed analysis of the effects of the three modes of material nature. He declares that the highest path of spirituality is pure, unconditional loving service unto the Supreme Divine Personality, Krishna. If we always remember Him, keep chanting His name and dedicate all our actions unto Him, take refuge in Him and make Him our Supreme goal, then by His grace, we will surely overcome all obstacles and difficulties and be freed from this cycle of birth and death.

verses.en: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: “O Sanjaya, what did my people and the Pāṇḍavas do, gathered together on the holy field of Kurukshetra, eager for battle?”
verses.hi: धृतराष्ट्र बोले - हे संजय! धर्मभूमि कुरुक्षेत्र में युद्ध की इच्छा से इकट्ठे हुए मेरेे और पाण्डु के पुत्रों ने भी क्या किया?
verses.short: Blind King Dhritarashtra asks: "What's happening on the battlefield?" The whole Gita is the answer to this one anxious question.
verses.commentary: Dharmakshetra -- that place which protects Dharma is Dharmakshetra. Because it was in the land of the Kurus, it was called Kurukshetra.Sanjaya is one who has conered likes and dislikes and who is impartial.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: King Duryodhana, upon seeing the Pandava army in battle array, approached his teacher Drona and said these words.
verses.hi: संजय बोले - उस समय वज्रव्यूह-से खड़ी हुई पाण्डव-सेना को देखकर राजा दुर्योधन द्रोणाचार्य के पास जाकर यह वचन बोला।
verses.short: Duryodhana sees the other army lined up and runs straight to his teacher. Nervous energy, trying to look confident.
verses.commentary: Sanjaya begins his report. Seeing the Pandava army arranged for battle, Duryodhana goes straight to his teacher Drona. Though he is king, he seeks out his teacher first, which hints at his unease. The story of the Gita opens with a leader who is worried before the fight has even started.

verses.en: Behold, O teacher, this mighty army of the Pandavas, arrayed by the son of Drupada, your intelligent disciple.
verses.hi: हे आचार्य! आपके बुद्धिमान् शिष्य द्रुपदपुत्र धृष्टद्युम्न के द्वारा व्यूहरचना से खड़ी की हुई पाण्डवों की इस बड़ी भारी सेना को देखिये
verses.short: "Look, teacher, your own student is leading their army." Duryodhana throwing subtle shade at Drona.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana points out the Pandava army, organised by Dhrishtadyumna, son of Drupada and once Drona's own student. There is a sting in his words: Drona trained the very man now leading the enemy. Duryodhana is subtly questioning his teacher's loyalty to rouse him.

verses.en: There (in that army) are heroes, great bowmen, such as Bhima and Arjuna; Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, a mighty warrior;
verses.hi: ।।1.4 -- 1.6।। यहाँ (पाण्डवों की सेना में) बड़े-बड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़े-बड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं। उनमें युयुधान (सात्यकि), राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं। धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं। पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोज--ये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं। पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं। सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं। ये सब-के-सब महारथी हैं।
verses.short: Duryodhana lists the legends on the other side: Bhima, Arjuna, and big names. He's lowkey scared.
verses.commentary: Technically, maharatha means a warrior who is proficient in the science of war and who is able to fight alone with ten thousand archers.

verses.en: Dhrstaketu, Cekitana, the valiant king of Kasi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Saibya, the best among men;
verses.hi: ।।1.4 -- 1.6।। यहाँ (पाण्डवों की सेना में) बड़े-बड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़े-बड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं। उनमें युयुधान (सात्यकि), राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं। धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं। पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोज--ये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं। पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं। सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं। ये सब-के-सब महारथी हैं।
verses.short: More heavy hitters on the Pandava side. Duryodhana keeps counting threats instead of trusting his own team.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana keeps naming great warriors on the Pandava side: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, the king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Shaibya. Each name adds to his sense of threat. The list shows how the Pandavas, though fewer, have gathered many respected allies.

verses.en: Yudhamanyu, the valiant one, and Uttamaujas, the strong one; and also the son of Subhadra, as well as the sons of Draupadi, all mighty warriors.
verses.hi: ।।1.4 -- 1.6।। यहाँ (पाण्डवों की सेना में) बड़े-बड़े शूरवीर हैं, जिनके बहुत बड़े-बड़े धनुष हैं तथा जो युद्ध में भीम और अर्जुनके समान हैं। उनमें युयुधान (सात्यकि), राजा विराट और महारथी द्रुपद भी हैं। धृष्टकेतु और चेकितान तथा पराक्रमी काशिराज भी हैं। पुरुजित् और कुन्तिभोज--ये दोनों भाई तथा मनुष्योंमें श्रेष्ठ शैब्य भी हैं। पराक्रमी युधामन्यु और पराक्रमी उत्तमौजा भी हैं। सुभद्रापुत्र अभिमन्यु और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र भी हैं। ये सब-के-सब महारथी हैं।
verses.short: Young warriors too, including Abhimanyu and Draupadi's sons. Every name makes Duryodhana more anxious.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana continues listing the Pandava champions, now naming the younger generation: Abhimanyu, son of Arjuna and Subhadra, and the five sons of Draupadi. His long roll call shows how anxious he is. Instead of trusting his own vast army, he keeps measuring himself against the strength of the other side.

verses.en: Know, O best of Brahmanas, those who are important on our side—those who are the commanders of my army. I shall name them to refresh your memory.
verses.hi: हे द्विजोत्तम! हमारे पक्ष में भी जो मुख्य हैं, उनपर भी आप ध्यान दीजिये। आपको याद दिलाने के लिये मेरी सेना के जो नायक हैं, उनको मैं कहता हूँ।
verses.short: Now he hypes his own side: "Let me remind you of our commanders." Classic pep talk to calm himself down.
verses.commentary: Having listed the enemy's heroes, Duryodhana turns to his own side to reassure his teacher Drona and, really, himself. Leaders who feel insecure often talk up their resources out loud. The scene shows a mind that depends on outside strength rather than inner conviction.

verses.en: Yourself, Bhisma, Karna, the victorious Krpa, Asvatthama, Vikarna, and Jayadratha, the son of Somadatta;
verses.hi: आप (द्रोणाचार्य) और पितामह भीष्म तथा कर्ण और संग्रामविजयी कृपाचार्य तथा वैसे ही अश्वत्थामा, विकर्ण और सोमदत्त का पुत्र भूरिश्रवा।
verses.short: Drona, Bhishma, Karna and more. Duryodhana flexing his roster like a fantasy team.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana names his great commanders: Drona himself, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashwatthama, Vikarna and Bhurishravas. These were among the most respected warriors of the age. Many of them fought for him out of duty or obligation rather than belief in his cause, which is part of the tragedy of the war.

verses.en: And there are many other heroes who are determined to give up their lives for my sake. They are all experts in using manifold missiles and dexterous in battle.
verses.hi: इनके अतिरिक्त बहुत-से शूरवीर हैं, जिन्होंने मेरे लिये अपने जीने की इच्छा का भी त्याग कर दिया है और जो अनेक प्रकार के शस्त्र-अस्त्रों को चलानेवाले हैं तथा जो सब-के-सब युद्धकला में अत्यन्त चतुर हैं।
verses.short: "So many heroes ready to die for me." When your confidence depends on others, it's shaky.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana adds that many other heroes are ready to give their lives for him, all skilled with many weapons. He takes comfort in the loyalty of others. Yet a confidence that rests entirely on other people's sacrifice is fragile.

verses.en: Our force is inadequate, guarded by Bhisma, while their force is adequate, guarded by Bhima.
verses.hi: वह हमारी सेना पाण्डवों पर विजय करने में अपर्याप्त है, असमर्थ है; क्योंकि उसके संरक्षक (उभयपक्षपाती) भीष्म हैं। परन्तु इन पाण्डवों की सेना हमारे पर विजय करने में पर्याप्त है, समर्थ है; क्योंकि इसके संरक्षक (निजसेनापक्षपाती) भीमसेन हैं।
verses.short: "Our army feels weak, theirs feels strong." Comparing yourself to others always messes with your head.
verses.commentary: The verse is differently interpreted by different commentators. Sridhara Swami takes the word aparyaptam to mean insufficient. Ananda Giri takes it to mean unlimited.

verses.en: Therefore, all of you, taking your places firmly in your respective divisions, should guard Bhisma at all costs.
verses.hi: आप सब-के-सब लोग सभी मोर्चों पर अपनी-अपनी जगह दृढ़ता से स्थित रहते हुए ही पितामह भीष्म की चारों ओर से रक्षा करें।
verses.short: "Everyone, protect Bhishma at all costs!" Duryodhana's whole plan rests on one person. Risky strategy.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana orders all his commanders to hold their positions and protect Bhishma above everything. His whole strategy rests on one elder. It reveals both his respect for Bhishma's power and his fear of what happens without him.

verses.en: Then the valiant grandsire Bhisma, the senior-most of the Kuru clan, roared like a lion and blew his conch with the intention of cheering up Duryodhana.
verses.hi: दुर्योधन के हृदय में हर्ष उत्पन्न करते हुए कुरुवृद्ध प्रभावशाली पितामह भीष्म ने सिंह के समान गरज कर जोर से शंख बजाया।
verses.short: Bhishma roars and blows his conch to boost Duryodhana's mood. The grandpa hype man moment.
verses.commentary: Seeing Duryodhana's nervousness, the elder Bhishma roars like a lion and blows his conch to lift his spirits. It is an act of loyalty and encouragement from the grand old man of the family. The conch blast also formally signals that the battle is about to begin.

verses.en: Then suddenly conchs, kettle drums, trumpets, tabors, and blow horns blared forth, and the sound was terrific.
verses.hi: उसके बाद शंख, भेरी (नगाड़े), ढोल, मृदङ्ग और नरसिंघे बाजे एक साथ बज उठे। उनका वह शब्द बड़ा भयंकर हुआ।
verses.short: Conches, drums, horns all at once. The noise is insane. Battle soundtrack: on.
verses.commentary: The whole Kaurava army answers Bhishma at once with conches, drums and horns, creating a deafening roar. The noise is meant to raise courage and frighten the enemy. Sanjaya describes the sound as tremendous, setting the charged atmosphere of the battlefield.

verses.en: Then Sri Krishna and Arjuna, stationed in their great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conchs.
verses.hi: उसके बाद सफेद घोड़ों से युक्त महान् रथ पर बैठे हुए लक्ष्मीपति भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण और पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने दिव्य शंखों को बड़े जोर से बजाया।
verses.short: Krishna and Arjuna, on a chariot with white horses, blow their divine conches. Main characters have entered.
verses.commentary: Now Krishna and Arjuna, standing in their magnificent chariot drawn by white horses, blow their divine conches. The white horses suggest purity and the divine conches suggest that this side has grace on its side. With Krishna as Arjuna's charioteer, the stage is set for the dialogue that follows.

verses.en: Sri Krishna blew his conch, Pancajanya, Arjuna his Devadatta, and Bhima of terrible deeds blew his great conch, Paundra.
verses.hi: अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने पाञ्चजन्य नामक तथा धनञ्जय अर्जुन ने देवदत्त नामक शंख बजाया; और भयानक कर्म करनेवाले वृकोदर भीम ने पौण्ड्र नामक महाशंख बजाया।
verses.short: Every hero has a named conch, like a signature sound. Krishna's is Panchajanya. Iconic.
verses.commentary: Each hero's conch has its own name, like a personal emblem. Krishna blows Panchajanya, Arjuna blows Devadatta, and the mighty Bhima blows Paundra. Naming them honours each warrior and shows the Pandavas answering the Kauravas with confidence.

verses.en: King Yudhisthira, the son of Kunti, blew his conch, Anantavijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew their conchs, Sughosa and Manipuspaka.
verses.hi: कुन्तीपुत्र राजा युधिष्ठिर ने अनन्तविजय नामक शंख बजाया तथा नकुल और सहदेव ने सुघोष और मणिपुष्पक नामक शंख बजाये।
verses.short: Yudhishthira, Nakula and Sahadeva join in. The Pandava brothers are fully in sync.
verses.commentary: The other Pandava brothers join in. Yudhishthira, the eldest, blows Anantavijaya, meaning endless victory, while the twins Nakula and Sahadeva blow Sughosha and Manipushpaka. The whole family stands united, each brother adding his voice.

verses.en: And the King of Kasi, the supreme bowman, Sikandi the mighty warrior, Dhrstadyumna, and Virata; and Satyaki, the invincible;
verses.hi: ।।1.17 -- 1.18।। हे राजन्! श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बी-लम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रा-पुत्र अभिमन्यु - इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलग-अलग (अपने-अपने) शंख बजाये।
verses.short: More warriors answer the call. The Pandava side is loud, united and ready.
verses.commentary: Sanjaya continues naming the Pandava allies who blow their conches: the king of Kashi, Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata and the unconquerable Satyaki. The roll call shows a united army answering with one voice.

verses.en: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, as well as the strong-armed son of Subhadra—all, O King, blew their respective conchs again and again.
verses.hi: ।।1.17 -- 1.18।। हे राजन्! श्रेष्ठ धनुषवाले काशिराज और महारथी शिखण्डी तथा धृष्टद्युम्न एवं राजा विराट और अजेय सात्यकि, राजा द्रुपद और द्रौपदी के पाँचों पुत्र तथा लम्बी-लम्बी भुजाओंवाले सुभद्रा-पुत्र अभिमन्यु - इन सभी ने सब ओर से अलग-अलग (अपने-अपने) शंख बजाये।
verses.short: Everyone blows their conch again and again. It's a full squad roll call.
verses.commentary: This blowing of conches announced the commencement of the battle.

verses.en: And that tumultuous uproar, reverberating through heaven and earth, rent the hearts of Dhrtarastra's sons.
verses.hi: पाण्डव-सेना के शंखों के उस भयंकर शब्द ने आकाश और पृथ्वी को भी गुँजाते हुए अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य हड़पनेवाले दुर्योधन आदि के हृदय विदीर्ण कर दिये।
verses.short: The sound shakes earth and sky, and the Kauravas feel it in their hearts. Unity is loud.
verses.commentary: The roar of the Pandava conches echoes across earth and sky and shakes the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons. A smaller army, united and confident, unsettles a larger one. Sanjaya hints to the blind king that his sons' courage is already wavering.

verses.en: Then Arjuna, whose banner crest was Hanuman, on beholding the sons of Dhrtarastra arrayed, took up his bow, while missiles were beginning to fly.
verses.hi: हे महीपते! धृतराष्ट्र! अब शस्त्रों के चलने की तैयारी हो ही रही थी कि उस समय अन्यायपूर्वक राज्य को धारण करनेवाले राजाओं और उनके साथियों को व्यवस्थितरूप से सामने खड़े हुए देखकर कपिध्वज पाण्डुपुत्र अर्जुन ने अपना गाण्डीव धनुष उठा लिया और अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण से ये वचन बोले।
verses.short: Arjuna, Hanuman on his flag, picks up his bow. The fight is about to begin.
verses.commentary: Arjuna, whose flag carries the image of Hanuman, sees the Kaurava army lined up and raises his bow as the first weapons are about to fly. Hanuman on the flag is a symbol of strength, devotion and divine protection. This is the last moment of certainty before Arjuna's crisis begins.

verses.en: And he spoke, O Lord of the Earth, these words to Sri Krishna: Arjuna said, “Draw up my chariot, O Krishna, between the two armies.
verses.hi: ।।1.21 -- 1.22।। अर्जुन बोले - हे अच्युत! दोनों सेनाओं के मध्य में मेरे रथ को आप तब तक खड़ा कीजिये, जब तक मैं युद्धक्षेत्र में खड़े हुए इन युद्ध की इच्छावालों को देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किन-किन के साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है।
verses.short: Arjuna: "Krishna, take my chariot to the middle." He wants a clear look before the battle.
verses.commentary: Arjuna asks Krishna to drive his chariot to the space between the two armies. Krishna, the Lord himself, has humbly taken the role of charioteer and follows his friend's instruction. Arjuna wants to see the battlefield clearly, not knowing that the view will shake him to the core.

verses.en: So that I may have a good look at those who are standing, eager to fight, and know with whom I must fight in this enterprise of war.
verses.hi: ।।1.21 -- 1.22।। अर्जुन बोले - हे अच्युत! दोनों सेनाओं के मध्य में मेरे रथ को आप तब तक खड़ा कीजिये, जब तक मैं युद्धक्षेत्र में खड़े हुए इन युद्ध की इच्छावालों को देख न लूँ कि इस युद्धरूप उद्योग में मुझे किन-किनके साथ युद्ध करना योग्य है।
verses.short: "Let me see who I'm actually up against." Smart move. Know what you're facing.
verses.commentary: Arjuna explains why he wants to stand between the armies: he wants to see exactly who he must fight. On the surface it is a warrior's practical wish to size up the enemy. Underneath, it sets up the moment when he recognises the faces of his own family.

verses.en: I wish to see those gathered here ready to fight in this battle in order to please the evil-minded son of Dhrtarashtra.
verses.hi: दुष्टबुद्धि दुर्योधन का युद्ध में प्रिय करने की इच्छावाले जो ये राजालोग इस सेना में आये हुए हैं, युद्ध करने को उतावले हुए इन सबको मैं देख लूँ।
verses.short: Arjuna wants to see who showed up to support Duryodhana's bad choices.
verses.commentary: Arjuna wants to see those who have gathered to support Duryodhana, whom he calls evil-minded. He still sees the battle in clear terms of right and wrong. That clarity is about to dissolve when he looks at the people standing there.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krishna drew up the best of chariots between the two armies, in full view of Bhisma, Drona, and all the other kings, O Dhrtarastra. He then said, "O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas."
verses.hi: ।।1.24 -- 1.25।। संजय बोले - हे भरतवंशी राजन्! निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथ को खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि 'हे पार्थ! इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख'।
verses.short: Krishna parks the chariot right in front of Bhishma and Drona and says: "Look at them." Plot twist loading.
verses.commentary: Krishna does as Arjuna asks and places the chariot in the middle of the battlefield. Sanjaya narrates this to the blind King Dhritarashtra, who is hearing the whole story second-hand. Krishna chooses the spot carefully, right in front of the elders Arjuna loves most.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krishna drew up the best of chariots between the two armies, in full view of Bhisma, Drona, and all the other kings, O Dhrtarastra. He then said, "O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas."
verses.hi: ।।1.24 -- 1.25।। संजय बोले - हे भरतवंशी राजन्! निद्राविजयी अर्जुन के द्वारा इस तरह कहने पर अन्तर्यामी भगवान् श्रीकृष्ण ने दोनों सेनाओं के मध्यभाग में पितामह भीष्म और आचार्य द्रोण के सामने तथा सम्पूर्ण राजाओं के सामने श्रेष्ठ रथको खड़ा करके इस तरह कहा कि 'हे पार्थ! इन इकट्ठे हुए कुरुवंशियोंको देख'।
verses.short: Krishna's "look at them" is deliberate. He knows exactly what Arjuna is about to feel.
verses.commentary: Positioned before Bhishma and Drona, Krishna simply says, "Arjuna, look at the Kurus gathered here." The words are few, but deliberate. By asking Arjuna to look, Krishna brings his hidden attachments to the surface so they can be addressed.

verses.en: Then, as Arjuna looked on, he saw standing there fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and comrades.
verses.hi: उसके बाद पृथानन्दन अर्जुनने उन दोनों ही सेनाओंमें स्थित पिताओंको, पितामहोंको, आचार्योंको, मामाओंको, भाइयोंको, पुत्रोंको, पौत्रोंको तथा मित्रोंको, ससुरोंको और सुहृदोंको भी देखा।
verses.short: Arjuna sees grandfathers, teachers, cousins, friends. The enemy is literally family.
verses.commentary: Arjuna looks and sees fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends on both sides. The enemy is no longer a faceless army. It is his own family and the people who raised and taught him.

verses.en: Fathers-in-law and dear friends in both armies, when Arjuna saw all these kinsmen arrayed,
verses.hi: अपनी-अपनी जगह पर स्थित उन सम्पूर्ण बान्धवों को देखकर वे कुन्तीनन्दन अर्जुन अत्यन्त कायरता से युक्त होकर विषाद करते हुए ये वचन बोले।
verses.short: In-laws and close friends on both sides. Suddenly this isn't a war. It's a family breakup.
verses.commentary: Seeing fathers-in-law and dear friends in both armies, Arjuna is overwhelmed. This is the turning point of the chapter. The warrior's resolve gives way to personal grief as he sees relationships rather than opponents.

verses.en: He was filled with deep compassion and said these words in despair:
verses.hi: ।।1.28 -- 1.30।। अर्जुन बोले - हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्ब-समुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं। हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है। मेरा मन भ्रमित-सा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ।
verses.short: Arjuna gets hit by a wave of emotion and starts to break down.
verses.commentary: Arjuna is filled with compassion and despair and begins to speak. The Gita describes his state as pity mixed with confusion. His feeling is human and understandable, but as Krishna will show, it is clouding his judgement about his duty.

verses.en: My limbs have weakened, my mouth has become parched, my body is trembling, and my hairs are standing on end.
verses.hi: ।।1.28 -- 1.30।। अर्जुन बोले - हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्ब-समुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं। हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है। मेरा मन भ्रमित-सा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ।
verses.short: Legs weak, mouth dry, body shaking, goosebumps. That's a full panic attack, described thousands of years ago.
verses.commentary: Arjuna describes his body giving way: his limbs feel weak, his mouth is dry, he is trembling and his hair stands on end. These are vivid signs of acute anxiety. The Gita does not hide the hero's breakdown; it starts the teaching exactly there.

verses.en: The bow Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin is burning. I can no longer stand. My mind seems to be reeling.
verses.hi: ।।1.28 -- 1.30।। अर्जुन बोले - हे कृष्ण! युद्ध की इच्छावाले इस कुटुम्ब-समुदाय को अपने सामने उपस्थित देखकर मेरे अङ्ग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और मुख सूख रहा है तथा मेरे शरीर में कँपकँपी आ रही है एवं रोंगटे खड़े हो रहे हैं। हाथ से गाण्डीव धनुष गिर रहा है और त्वचा भी जल रही है। मेरा मन भ्रमित-सा हो रहा है और मैं खड़े रहने में भी असमर्थ हो रहा हूँ।
verses.short: His bow slips, his skin burns, his head spins. Even the greatest warrior can hit a wall.
verses.commentary: His great bow Gandiva slips from his hand, his skin burns, he cannot stand steady and his mind spins. The strongest warrior of his time is completely overwhelmed. The verse shows that physical strength is no protection when the mind is in turmoil.

verses.en: I see, Kṛṣṇa, inauspicious omens. I foresee no good in slaying my kinsmen in battle.
verses.hi: हे केशव! मैं लक्षणों  - (शकुनों) को भी विपरीत देख रहा हूँ और युद्ध में स्वजनोंको मारकर श्रेय (लाभ) भी नहीं देख रहा हूँ।
verses.short: "I only see bad signs. Nothing good comes from killing my own people."
verses.commentary: Arjuna says he sees only bad omens and can find no good in killing his own people. His mind now looks for reasons to support what his emotions already feel. This is a common pattern: when we are distressed, we read the signs to confirm our fears.

verses.en: I desire no victory, nor empire, nor pleasures. What have we to do with empire, O Krishna, or enjoyment, or even life?
verses.hi: हे कृष्ण! मैं न तो विजय चाहता हूँ, न राज्य चाहता हूँ और न सुखों को ही चाहता हूँ। हे गोविन्द! हमलोगों को राज्य से क्या लाभ? भोगों से क्या लाभ? अथवा जीने से भी क्या लाभ?
verses.short: "I don't want the win, the throne or the luxury. What's the point of any of it?" Total burnout energy.
verses.commentary: Arjuna says he wants no victory, kingdom or pleasure, and asks what any of it is worth. It sounds like renunciation, but it comes from grief rather than wisdom. Krishna will later teach the difference between letting go out of clarity and giving up out of despair.

verses.en: Those for whose sake we desire empire, enjoyment, and pleasures, stand here in war, renouncing life and wealth.
verses.hi: जिनके लिये हमारी राज्य, भोग और सुखकी इच्छा है, वे ही ये सब अपने प्राणों की और धन की आशा का त्याग करके युद्ध में खड़े हैं।
verses.short: "The people I'd want to share the success with are the ones standing here to fight."
verses.commentary: Arjuna points out that the very people for whom one wants a kingdom and its joys are standing here, ready to give up their lives and wealth. Without them, success would feel empty. His love for his family is real, which is what makes his dilemma so painful.

verses.en:
all these are to be regarded as one's own self.

Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other kinsmen—all these are to be regarded as one's own self.
verses.hi: ।।1.34 -- 1.35।। आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और उसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं, मुझ पर प्रहार करने पर भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, और हे मधुसूदन! मुझे त्रिलोकी का राज्य मिलता हो, तो भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, फिर पृथ्वी के लिये तो (मैं इनको मारूँ ही) क्या?
verses.short: Teachers, fathers, sons, uncles, in-laws: Arjuna sees them all as his own people. That's the pain.
verses.commentary: Arjuna lists teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws and other relatives, all standing ready to fight. He sees every one of them as his own. The repetition of family words shows how personal the war has become for him.

verses.en: I would not slay them, even if they might slay me, for the sovereignty of the three worlds—how much less for this earth, O Krsna?
verses.hi: ।।1.34 -- 1.35।। आचार्य, पिता, पुत्र और उसी प्रकार पितामह, मामा, ससुर, पौत्र, साले तथा अन्य जितने भी सम्बन्धी हैं, मुझपर प्रहार करने पर भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, और हे मधुसूदन! मुझे त्रिलोकी का राज्य मिलता हो, तो भी मैं इनको मारना नहीं चाहता, फिर पृथ्वीके लिये तो (मैं इनको मारूँ ही) क्या?
verses.short: "Even for all three worlds I wouldn't kill them, let alone for this earth."
verses.commentary: Arjuna says he would not kill his kinsmen even if they tried to kill him, not even for rule over the three worlds, let alone this earth. His love overrides any thought of gain. It is a noble feeling, but it leaves no room for his responsibility to stand against injustice.

verses.en: If we were to kill the sons of Dhrtarastra, what joy would be ours, O Krsna? Sin alone would accrue to us if we killed these murderous felons.
verses.hi: हे जनार्दन! इन धृतराष्ट्र-सम्बन्धियों को मारकर हमलोगों को क्या प्रसन्नता होगी? इन आततायियों को मारने से तो हमें पाप ही लगेगा।
verses.short: "Even if they're wrong, what joy is there in destroying them? It'll only leave guilt."
verses.commentary: Janardana means one who is worshipped by all for prosperity and salvation -- Krishna.He who sets fire to the house of another, who gives poision, who runs with sword to kill, who has plundered wealth and lands, and who has taken hold of the wife of somody else is an atatayi. Duryodhana had done all these evil actions.

verses.en: Therefore, it is not befitting for us to slay our kin, the sons of Dhrtarastra. For if we kill our kinsmen, O Krsna, how can we be happy?
verses.hi: इसलिये अपने बान्धव इन धृतराष्ट्र-सम्बन्धियों को मारने के लिये हम योग्य नहीं हैं; क्योंकि हे माधव! अपने कुटुम्बियों को मारकर हम कैसे सुखी होंगे?
verses.short: "How could we ever be happy after killing our own family?" Arjuna's heart is overruling everything.
verses.commentary: Arjuna concludes that it is not right to kill their own relatives, asking how they could ever be happy after that. He measures the choice only by how it will feel afterwards. Krishna will later teach him to judge action by duty rather than by expected happiness.

verses.en: Though these people, whose minds are overpowered by greed, see no evil in the destruction of a clan and no sin in treachery to friends,
verses.hi: ।।1.38 -- 1.39।। यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेक-विचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये (दुर्योधन आदि) कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, (तो भी) हे जनार्दन! कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीक-ठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होने का विचार क्यों न करें?
verses.short: "They're blinded by greed and don't see the damage. But we can see it."
verses.commentary: Arjuna acknowledges that the Kauravas, blinded by greed, see nothing wrong in destroying their family or betraying friends. He believes that seeing the wrong clearly should keep him from joining in. His logic sounds moral, but it ignores that standing aside also has consequences.

verses.en: Why should we not learn to shun this crime—we who see the evil of ruining a clan, O Krishna?
verses.hi: ।।1.38 -- 1.39।। यद्यपि लोभ के कारण जिनका विवेक-विचार लुप्त हो गया है, ऐसे ये (दुर्योधन आदि) कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को और मित्रों के साथ द्वेष करने से होनेवाले पाप को नहीं देखते, (तो भी) हे जनार्दन! कुल का नाश करने से होनेवाले दोष को ठीक-ठीक जाननेवाले हमलोग इस पाप से निवृत्त होनेका विचार क्यों न करें?
verses.short: "If we know this is wrong, why shouldn't we walk away?" Arjuna building his case to quit.
verses.commentary: Ignorance of law is no excuse but wanton sinful conduct is a grave crime, unworthy of us, who are wiser.

verses.en: With the ruin of a clan, its ancient traditions perish, and when traditions perish, lawlessness overtakes the whole clan.
verses.hi: कुल का क्षय होने पर सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं और धर्म का नाश होनेपर (बचे हुए) सम्पूर्ण कुल को अधर्म दबा लेता है।
verses.short: "When families fall apart, traditions and values go with them, and chaos follows."
verses.commentary: Dharma -- the duties and ceremonies practised by the family in accordance with the injunctions of the scriptures.

verses.en: When lawlessness prevails, O Krsna, the women of the clan become corrupted; when women become corrupted, there arises an intermixing of classes.
verses.hi: हे कृष्ण! अधर्म के अधिक बढ़ जाने से कुल की स्त्रियाँ दूषित हो जाती हैं; (और) हे वार्ष्णेय! स्त्रियों के दूषित होने पर वर्णसंकर पैदा हो जाते हैं।
verses.short: Arjuna worries society will lose its moral compass if this war happens. Big-picture fear.
verses.commentary: Arjuna warns that when lawlessness spreads, the moral fabric of families weakens and social order breaks down. He is worried about the long-term damage war does to society. The fear is genuine, though it is being used to justify walking away from his duty.

verses.en: This mixing of classes leads to hell for the clan itself and its destroyers; for the spirits of their ancestors fall degraded, deprived of the ritual offerings of food and water.
verses.hi: वर्णसंकर कुलघातियों को और कुल को नरक में ले जानेवाला ही होता है। श्राद्ध और तर्पण न मिलने से इन- (कुलघातियों-) के पितर भी अपने स्थान से गिर जाते हैं।
verses.short: He fears the damage will hit generations, even the ancestors. His anxiety is now going full worst-case.
verses.commentary: Arjuna argues that the collapse of family order harms everyone, even the ancestors, who would lose the rites and offerings meant for them. He is using tradition and religion to justify his reluctance to fight. His reasoning is sincere, but it is driven by grief.

verses.en: By the sins of the clan-destroyers who bring about intermixing of classes, the ancient traditions of the clans and classes are destroyed.
verses.hi: इन वर्णसंकर पैदा करनेवाले दोषोंसे कुलघातियों के सदा से चलते आये कुलधर्म और जातिधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं।
verses.short: "Those who break families destroy traditions that took ages to build."
verses.commentary: Arjuna continues that those who destroy families also destroy long-standing traditions and social values. He fears the war will leave society without its moral anchors. The concern is serious, but Krishna will show that abandoning his duty is not the answer.

verses.en: For those whose clan laws are destroyed, dwelling in hell is ordained, O Krishna; thus, we have heard.
verses.hi: हे जनार्दन! जिनके कुलधर्म नष्ट हो जाते हैं, उन मनुष्यों का बहुत काल तक नरकों में वापस होता है, ऐसा हम सुनते आये हैं।
verses.short: "We've heard that people who destroy family values suffer badly." Fear is doing the talking now.
verses.commentary: Arjuna cites what he has heard: those who destroy family traditions suffer for a long time afterwards. He is building a case from scripture and custom. Fear of consequences now dominates his thinking.

verses.en: Alas! We have resolved to commit a great sin, for we are ready to slay our kin out of desire for sovereignty and enjoyment.
verses.hi: यह बड़े आश्चर्य और खेद की बात है कि हमलोग बड़ा भारी पाप करने का निश्चय कर बैठे हैं, जो कि राज्य और सुख के लोभ से अपने स्वजनों को मारने के लिये तैयार हो गये हैं!
verses.short: "We're about to do something terrible just for power and comfort." Guilt hits hard.
verses.commentary: Arjuna cries out that they are about to commit a great wrong just to win a kingdom and its pleasures. Guilt has taken over completely. He frames the whole war as selfish ambition, forgetting the injustice that made it necessary.

verses.en: If the well-armed sons of Dhrtarastra should slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be better for me.
verses.hi: अगर ये हाथों में शस्त्र-अस्त्र लिये हुए धृतराष्ट्र के पक्षपाती लोग युद्धभूमि में सामना न करनेवाले तथा शस्त्ररहित मुझ को मार भी दें, तो वह मेरे लिये बड़ा ही हितकारक होगा।
verses.short: "I'd rather let them kill me, unarmed, than fight." Arjuna is ready to give up completely.
verses.commentary: Arjuna says it would be better if the Kauravas killed him while he stood unarmed and did not resist. This is the lowest point of his despair. He would rather give up his life than face the choice in front of him.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus on the battlefield, Arjuna threw aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot seat, his heart overwhelmed with grief.
verses.hi: संजय बोले - ऐसा कहकर शोकाकुल मनवाले अर्जुन बाणसहित धनुष का त्याग करके युद्धभूमि में रथके मध्यभाग में बैठ गये।
verses.short: Arjuna drops his bow, sits down, and breaks. Rock bottom. And this is exactly where the Gita begins.
verses.commentary: Having spoken, Arjuna drops his bow and arrows and sinks down in the chariot, overwhelmed with sorrow. The first chapter ends with the hero collapsed. This is called the yoga of Arjuna's despair because the crisis itself becomes the doorway to wisdom.

verses.en: Sanjaya said: To him, who was overcome with pity, whose eyes were wet with tears, who was sorrow-stricken and bore a bewildered look, Sri Krishna spoke as follows:
verses.hi: संजय बोले - वैसी कायरता से आविष्ट उन अर्जुन के प्रति, जो कि विषाद कर रहे हैं और आँसुओं के कारण जिनके नेत्रों की देखने की शक्ति अवरुद्ध हो रही है, भगवान् मधुसूदन ये (आगे कहे जानेवाले) वचन बोले।
verses.short: Arjuna's crying, overwhelmed, frozen. Krishna sees it all and steps in. Big talk incoming.
verses.commentary: Sanjaya describes Arjuna overcome with pity, his eyes full of tears, deeply distressed. It is to this broken Arjuna that Krishna now speaks. The teaching of the Gita begins not in a calm classroom but in a moment of real crisis.

verses.en: The Lord said, "Whence comes this despondency upon you, O Arjuna, in this crisis? It is unfitting for a noble person; it is disgraceful and it obstructs one's attainment of heaven."
verses.hi: श्रीभगवान् बोले - हे अर्जुन! इस विषम अवसरपर तुम्हें यह कायरता कहाँसे प्राप्त हुई, जिसका कि श्रेष्ठ पुरुष सेवन नहीं करते, जो स्वर्गको देनेवाली नहीं है और कीर्ति करनेवाली भी नहीं है।
verses.short: Krishna: "Bro, why are you breaking down right now? This isn't you, and it won't get you anywhere."
verses.commentary: Krishna's first words are a challenge: where has this weakness come from at such a critical moment? He says it does not suit a noble person and leads neither to honour nor to the higher good. Before offering comfort, Krishna shakes Arjuna out of his spiral.

verses.en: Do not yield to unmanliness, O Arjuna, it does not befit you. Shake off this base faint-heartedness and arise, O conqueror of foes!
verses.hi: हे पृथानन्दन अर्जुन ! इस नपुंसकताको मत प्राप्त हो; क्योंकि तुम्हारेमें यह उचित नहीं है। हे परंतप ! हृदयकी इस तुच्छ दुर्बलताका त्याग करके युद्धके लिये खड़े हो जाओ।
verses.short: This isn't you. Stop doom-spiralling, get up, and handle it. You're bigger than this moment.
verses.commentary: Krishna urges Arjuna not to give in to faint-heartedness, saying it does not befit him. He tells him to shake off this weakness of heart and stand up. It is a call to remember who he really is and to act from strength rather than fear.

verses.en: Arjuna said, "O slayer of foes, how can I aim arrows in battle against Bhisma and Drona, who are worthy of reverence?"
verses.hi: अर्जुन बोले - हे मधुसूदन! मैं रणभूमिमें भीष्म और द्रोणके साथ बाणोंसे युद्ध कैसे करूँ? क्योंकि हे अरिसूदन! ये दोनों ही पूजाके योग्य हैं।
verses.short: Arjuna: "How do I fight people I literally look up to?" Real dilemma, real pain.
verses.commentary: Arjuna replies by asking how he could possibly shoot arrows at Bhishma and Drona, who deserve his worship. His question is honest. He cannot reconcile his duty as a warrior with his love and reverence for his elders.

verses.en: It is better even to live on a beggar's fare in this world than to slay these most venerable teachers. If I were to slay my teachers, though they may be degraded by desire for wealth, I would only be enjoying blood-stained pleasures here.
verses.hi: महानुभाव गुरुजनोंको न मारकर इस लोकमें मैं भिक्षाका अन्न खाना भी श्रेष्ठ समझता हूँ।  क्योंकि गुरुजनोंको मारकर यहाँ रक्तसे सने हुए तथा धनकी कामनाकी मुख्यतावाले भोगोंको ही तो भोगूँगा!
verses.short: Arjuna would rather be broke than hurt his teachers. Any win built on that feels toxic to him.
verses.commentary: Arjuna says it would be better to live by begging than to kill his revered teachers. Any wealth or pleasure won by their death would feel stained with blood. His values are sincere, but they are being tested by a situation with no easy answer.

verses.en: We do not know which of the two is better for us: whether our vanquishing them or their vanquishing us. The very sons of Dhrtarastra, whom, if we were to slay, we would not wish to live, even they are standing in array against us.
verses.hi: हम यह भी नहीं जानते कि हमलोगोंके लिये युद्ध करना और न करना - इन दोनोंमेंसे कौन-सा अत्यन्त श्रेष्ठ है; और हमें इसका भी पता नहीं है कि हम उन्हें जीतेंगे अथवा वे हमें जीतेंगे। जिनको मारकर हम जीना भी नहीं चाहते, वे ही धृतराष्ट्रके सम्बन्धी हमारे सामने खड़े हैं।
verses.short: Arjuna doesn't even know what winning means anymore. Win or lose, someone he loves gets hurt.
verses.commentary: Arjuna admits he does not even know which outcome would be better, winning or losing. If he kills his cousins, he would not want to live. This uncertainty is the heart of his crisis and the reason he finally turns to Krishna for help.

verses.en: With my heart stricken by the fault of weak compassion, my mind perplexed about my duty, I implore you to tell me for certain what is good for me. I am your disciple; teach me, who have taken refuge in you.
verses.hi: कायरतारूप दोषसे तिरस्कृत स्वभाववाला और धर्मके विषयमें मोहित अन्तःकरणवाला मैं आपसे पूछता हूँ कि जो निश्चित कल्याण करनेवाली हो, वह मेरे लिये कहिये। मैं आपका शिष्य हूँ। आपके शरण हुए मुझे शिक्षा दीजिये।
verses.short: Arjuna finally admits: "I'm confused. I need help. Guide me." Asking for help is the first real step.
verses.commentary: Arjuna confesses that weakness and confusion have overpowered him and asks Krishna to tell him clearly what is best. He says, "I am your disciple; teach me, I surrender to you." This moment of humility transforms the conversation. Krishna's teaching begins because Arjuna asks.

verses.en: Even if I were to win unchallenged sovereignty of a prosperous earth or even lordship over the Devas, I do not feel that it would dispel the grief that withers up my senses.
verses.hi: पृथ्वीपर धन-धान्य-समृद्ध और शत्रुरहित राज्य तथा स्वर्गमें देवताओंका आधिपत्य मिल जाय तो भी इन्द्रियोंको सुखानेवाला मेरा जो शोक है, वह दूर हो जाय - ऐसा मैं नहीं देखता हूँ।
verses.short: Even owning the whole world wouldn't fix this pain. Money and power can't heal a confused mind.
verses.commentary: Arjuna says that even a flourishing kingdom on earth or rule over the gods would not remove the grief drying up his senses. He has realised that outer success cannot heal inner pain. That realisation opens him to deeper wisdom.

verses.en: Sanjaya said, Having thus spoken to Sri Krsna, Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep and the scorcher of foes, said, "I will not fight," and became silent.
verses.hi: संजय बोले - हे शत्रुतापन धृतराष्ट्र! ऐसा कहकर निद्राको जीतनेवाले अर्जुन अन्तर्यामी भगवान् गोविन्दसे 'मैं युद्ध नहीं करूँगा' ऐसा साफ-साफ कहकर चुप हो गये।
verses.short: Arjuna says "I won't fight" and goes silent. Full shutdown mode.
verses.commentary: Sanjaya reports that Arjuna, after speaking, declares "I will not fight" and falls silent. He has said everything he can. His silence makes space for Krishna's teaching to begin.

verses.en: O King, to him who was thus sorrowing between the two armies, Sri Krishna spoke the following words, as if smiling (by way of ridicule).
verses.hi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव धृतराष्ट्र! दोनों सेनाओंके मध्यभागमें विषाद करते हुए उस अर्जुनके प्रति हँसते हुए-से भगवान् हृषीकेश यह (आगे कहे जानेवाले) वचन बोले।
verses.short: Krishna smiles. Not mocking, just calm. He knows this crisis is where the growth starts.
verses.commentary: Sanjaya tells the king that Krishna, standing between the two armies, smiles gently and speaks to the grieving Arjuna. The smile is not mockery but calm reassurance. Krishna can see beyond the crisis to the clarity Arjuna is about to gain.

verses.en: The Lord said, "You grieve for those who should not be grieved for; yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living."
verses.hi: श्रीभगवान् बोले - तुमने शोक न करनेयोग्यका शोक किया है और  पण्डिताईकी बातें कह रहे हो; परन्तु जिनके प्राण चले गये हैं, उनके लिये और जिनके प्राण नहीं गये हैं, उनके लिये पण्डितलोग शोक नहीं करते।
verses.short: You're overthinking things that don't deserve your grief. Wise people don't spiral over life or death.
verses.commentary: The philosophy of the Gita begins from this verse.Bhishma and Drona deserve no grief because they are eternal in their real nature and they are virtuous men who possess very good conduct. Though you speak words of wisdom, you are unwise because you grieve for those who are really eternal and who deserve no grief. They who are endowed with the knowledge of the Self are wise men. They will not grieve for the living or for the dead because they know well that the Self is immortal and that It is unborn. They also know that there is no such a thing as death, that it is a separation of the astral body from the physical, that death is nothing more than a disintegration of matter and that the five elements of which the body is composed return to their source. Arjuna had forgotten the eternal nature of the Soul and the changing nature of the body. Because of his ignorance, he began to act as if the temporary relations with kinsmen, teachers, etc., were permanent. He forgot that his relations with this world in his present life were the results of past actions. These, when exhausted, end all relationship and new ones ones crop up when one takes on another body.The result of past actions is known as karm and that portion of the karma which gave rise to the present incarnation is known as prarabdha karma.

verses.en: There never was a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings. Nor will there be any time in the future when all of us shall cease to exist.
verses.hi: किसी कालमें मैं नहीं था और तू नहीं था तथा ये राजालोग नहीं थे, यह बात भी नहीं है; और इसके बाद (भविष्य में) मैं, तू और राजलोग - हम सभी नहीं रहेंगे, यह बात भी नहीं है।
verses.short: You, me, everyone here: we always existed and always will. You're not as temporary as you think.
verses.commentary: Lord Krishna speaks here of the immortality of the Soul or the imperishable nature of the Self (Atman). The Soul exists in the three periods of time (past, present and future). Man continues to exist even after the death of the physical body. There is life beyond.

verses.en: Just as the self associated with a body passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so too, at death, it passes into another body. A wise man is not deluded by that.
verses.hi: देहधारीके इस मनुष्यशरीरमें जैसे बालकपन, जवानी और वृद्धावस्था होती है, ऐसे ही देहान्तरकी प्राप्ति होती है। उस विषयमें धीर मनुष्य मोहित नहीं होता।
verses.short: Childhood, teen years, old age, then a new body. You keep upgrading; the real you stays.
verses.commentary: Just as there is no interruption in the passing of childhood into youth and youth into old age in this body, so also there is no interruption by death in the continuity of the ego. The Self is not dead at the termination of the stage, viz., childhood. It is certainly not born again at the beginning of the second stage, viz., youth. Just as the Self passes unchanged from childhood to youth and from yourth to old age, so also the Self passes unchanged from one body into,another. Therefore, the wise man is not at all distressed about it.

verses.en: The contact of the senses with their objects, O Arjuna, gives rise to feelings of cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, never lasting long. Endure them, O Arjuna.
verses.hi: हे कुन्तीनन्दन! इन्द्रियोंके जो विषय (जड पदार्थ) हैं, वो तो शीत (अनुकूलता) और उष्ण (प्रतिकूलता) - के द्वारा सुख और दुःख देनेवाले हैं तथा आने-जानेवाले और अनित्य हैं। हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन! उनको तुम सहन करो।
verses.short: Feelings come and go like weather. One bad day isn't your whole story. Let it pass and keep going.
verses.commentary: Cold is pleasant at one time and painful at another. Heat is pleasant in winter but painful in summer. The same object that gives pleasure at one time gives pain at another time. So the sensecontacts that give rise to the sensations of heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. Therefore, they are impermanent in nature. The objects come in contact with the senses or the Indriyas, viz., skin, ear, eye, nose, etc., and the sensations are carried by the nerves to the mind which has its seat in the brain. It is the mind that feels pleasure and pain. One should try to bear patiently heat and cold, pleasure and pain and develop a balanced state of mind. (Cf.V.22)

verses.en: For, he whom these do not affect, O chief of men, and to whom pain and pleasure are equal - that steadfast man alone is worthy of immortality.
verses.hi: कारण कि हे पुरुषोंमें श्रेष्ठ अर्जुन! सुख-दुःखमें सम रहनेवाले जिस धीर मनुष्यको ये मात्रास्पर्श (पदार्थ) व्यथित (सुखी-दुःखी) नहीं कर पाते, वह अमर होनेमें समर्थ हो जाता है अर्थात् वह अमर हो जाता है।
verses.short: Stay the same whether it's pain or pleasure. That steady person can't be shaken by anything.
verses.commentary: Dehadhyasa or identification of the Self with the body is the cause of pleasure and pain. The more you are able to identify yourself with the immortal, allpervading Self, the less will you be affected by the pairs of opposites (Dvandvas, pleasure and pain, etc.)Titiksha or the power of endurance develops the willpower. Calm endurance in pleasure and pain, and heat and cold is one of the alifications of an aspirant on the path of Jnana Yoga. It is one of the Shatsampat or sixfold virtues. It is a condition of right knowledge. Titiksha by itself cannot give you Moksha or liberation, but still, when coupled with discrimination and dispassion, it becomes a means to the attainment of Immortality or knowledge of the Self. (Cf.XVII.53)

verses.en: The unreal never comes into being, the real never ceases to be. The truth about these two is seen by the seers.
verses.hi: असत् का तो भाव (सत्ता) विद्यमान नहीं है और सत् का अभाव विद्यमान नहीं है, तत्त्वदर्शी महापुरुषोंने इन दोनोंका ही अन्त अर्थात् तत्त्व देखा है।
verses.short: What's fake never really exists. What's real never disappears. Learn to tell the difference.
verses.commentary: The changeless, homogeneous Atman or the Self always exists. It is the only solid Reality. This phenomenal world of names and forms is ever changing. Hence it is unreal. The sage or the Jivanmukta is fully aware that the Self always exists and that this world is like a mirage. Through his Jnanachakshus or the eye of intuition, he directly cognises the Self. This world vanishes for him like the snake in the rope, after it has been seen that only the rope exists. He rejects the names and forms and takes the underlying Essence in all the names and forms, viz., AstiBhatiPriya or Satchidananda or ExistenceKnowledgeBliss Absolute. Hence he is a Tattvadarshi or a knower of the Truth or the Essence.What is changing must be unreal. What is constant or permanent must be real.

verses.en: Know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. No one can cause the destruction of this immutable.
verses.hi: अविनाशी तो उसको जान, जिससे यह सम्पूर्ण संसार व्याप्त है। इस अविनाशीका विनाश कोई भी नहीं कर सकता।
verses.short: The thing that runs through everything can't be destroyed. Nobody can delete the real you.
verses.commentary: Krishna points to the reality that pervades everything and says it can never be destroyed. Bodies and situations change, but that underlying presence does not. No one has the power to destroy the imperishable. This is the first step in removing Arjuna's grief about death.

verses.en: These bodies of the Jiva (the embodied self) are said to have an end, while the Jiva itself is eternal, indestructible, and incomprehensible. Therefore, fight, O Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.hi: अविनाशी, अप्रमेय और नित्य रहनेवाले इस शरीरी के ये देह अन्तवाले कहे गये हैं। इसलिये हे अर्जुन! तुम युद्ध करो।
verses.short: Bodies have an expiry date. The soul doesn't. So do what you have to do.
verses.commentary: Lord Krishna explains to Arjuna the nature of the allpervading, immortal Self in a variety of ways and thus induces him to fight by removing his delusion, grief and despondency which are born of ignorance.

verses.en: He who considers It (the self) to be the slayer, and he who thinks of It as slain—both are ignorant. For, the self neither slays nor is being slain.
verses.hi: जो मनुष्य इस अविनाशी शरीरीको मारनेवाला मानता है और जो मनुष्य इसको मरा मानता है, वे दोनों ही इसको नहीं जानते; क्योंकि यह न मारता है और न मारा जाता है।
verses.short: Thinking the soul kills or gets killed? Both takes are wrong. It's untouchable.
verses.commentary: The Self is nondoer (Akarta) and as It is immutable, It is neither the agent nor the object of the act of slaying. He who thinks I slay or I am slain with the body or the Ahamkara (ego), he does not really comprehend the true nature of the Self. The Self is indestructible. It exists in the three periods of time. It is Sat (Existence). When the body is destroyed, the Self is not destroyed. The body has to undergo change in any case. It is inevitable. But the Self is not at all affected by it. Verses 19, 20, 21, 23 and 24 speak of the immortality of the Self or Atman. (Cf.XVIII.17)

verses.en: It is never born; it never dies; having come into existence once, it never ceases to exist. Unborn, eternal, perpetual, and primordial, it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.
verses.hi: यह शरीरी न कभी जन्मता है और न मरता है तथा यह उत्पन्न होकर फिर होनेवाला नहीं है। यह जन्मरहित, नित्य-निरन्तर रहनेवाला, शाश्वत और पुराण (अनादि) है। शरीरके मारे जानेपर भी यह नहीं मारा जाता।
verses.short: The real you was never born and can't die. Bodies change, but the one watching it all stays.
verses.commentary: This Self (Atman) is destitute of the six types of transformation or BhavaVikaras such as birth, existence, growth, transformation, decline and death. As It is indivisible (Akhanda). It does not diminish in size. It neither grows nor does It decline. It is ever the same. Birth and death are for the physical body only. Birth and death cannot touch the immortal, allpervading Self.

verses.en: He who knows this self to be indestructible, unborn, unchanging, and thus eternal—how, O Arjuna, does he cause anyone to be killed, and whom does he kill?
verses.hi: हे पृथानन्दन! जो मनुष्य इस शरीरीको अविनाशी, नित्य, जन्मरहित और अव्यय जानता है, वह कैसे किसको मारे और कैसे किसको मरवाये?
verses.short: Once you know the soul can't be destroyed, the whole fear of killing and dying changes.
verses.commentary: The enlightened sage who knows the immutable and indestructible Self through direct cognition or spiritual Anubhava (experience) cannot do the act of slaying. He cannot cause another to slay also.

verses.en: As a man casts off worn-out garments and puts on new ones, so does the embodied self cast off its worn-out bodies and enter into new ones.
verses.hi: मनुष्य जैसे पुराने कपड़ोंको छोड़कर दूसरे नये कपड़े धारण कर लेता है, ऐसे ही देही पुराने शरीरोंको छोड़कर दूसरे नये शरीरोंमें चला जाता है।
verses.short: Changing bodies is like changing clothes. Old fit off, new fit on. Same you inside.
verses.commentary: Krishna compares death to changing clothes. Just as we throw away worn-out clothes and put on new ones, the self leaves worn-out bodies and takes on new ones. The image makes death feel less like an ending and more like a transition.

verses.en: Weapons cannot cleave It, fire cannot burn It, waters cannot wet It, and wind cannot dry It.
verses.hi: शस्त्र इस शरीरीको काट नहीं सकते, अग्नि इसको जला नहीं सकती, जल इसको गीला नहीं कर सकता और वायु इसको सुखा नहीं सकती।
verses.short: Weapons can't cut it, fire can't burn it, water can't wet it, wind can't dry it. Built different.
verses.commentary: The Self is indivisible. It has no parts. It is extremely subtle. It is infinite. Therefore, sword cannot cut It fire cannot burn It water cannot wet It wind cannot dry It.

verses.en: It cannot be cleaved; It cannot be burned; It cannot be wetted, and It cannot be dried; It is eternal, all-pervasive, stable, immovable, and primordial.
verses.hi: यह शरीरी काटा नहीं जा सकता, यह जलाया नहीं जा सकता, यह गीला नहीं किया जा सकता और यह सुखाया भी नहीं जा सकता। कारण कि यह नित्य रहनेवाला सबमें परिपूर्ण, अचल, स्थिर स्वभाववाला और अनादि है।
verses.short: The soul can't be cut, burned, soaked or dried. It's everywhere, steady, and forever.
verses.commentary: The Self is very subtle. It is beyond the reach of speech and mind. It is very difficult to understand this subtle Self. So Lord Krishna explains the nature of the immortal Self in a variety of ways with various illustrations and examples, so that It can be grasped by the people.Sword cannot cut this Self. It is eternal. Because It is eternal, It is allpervading. Because It is allpervading, It is stable like a stature. Because It is stable, It is immovable. It is everlasting. Therefore, It is not produced out of any cause. It is not new. It is ancient.

verses.en: This (self) is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable, and unchanging. Therefore, knowing it thus, it does not befit you to grieve.
verses.hi: यह देही प्रत्यक्ष नहीं दीखता, यह चिन्तनका विषय नहीं है और यह निर्विकार कहा जाता है। अतः इस देहीको ऐसा जानकर शोक नहीं करना चाहिये।
verses.short: You can't see it or fully figure it out, and it never changes. So stop grieving.
verses.commentary: The Self is not an object of perception. It can hardly be seen by the physical eyes. Therefore, the Self is unmanifested. That which is seen by the eyes becomes an object of thought. As the Self cannot be perceived by the eyes, It is unthinkable. Milk when mixed with buttermilk changes its form. The Self cannot change Its form like milk. Hence, It is changeless and immutable. Therefore, thus understanding the Self, thou shouldst not mourn. Thou shouldst not think also that thou art their slayer and that they are killed by thee.

verses.en: Or, if you consider this self as constantly being born and constantly dying, O mighty-armed one, it still does not become you to feel grief.
verses.hi: हे महाबाहो ! अगर तुम इस देहीको नित्य पैदा होनेवाला अथवा नित्य मरनेवाला भी मानो, तो भी तुम्हें इस प्रकार शोक नहीं करना चाहिये।
verses.short: Even if you think the soul dies every time, grieving still doesn't help. Stay strong.
verses.commentary: Lord Krishna here, for the sake of argument, takes up the popular supposition. Granting that the Self is again and again born whenever a body comes into being, and again and again dies whenever the body dies, O mightyarmed (O Arjuna of great valour and strength), thou shouldst not grieve thus, because birth is inevitable to want is dead and death is inevitable to what is born. This is the inexorable or unrelenting Law of Nature.

verses.en: For, death is certain for the born, and rebirth is certain for the dead; therefore, you should not grieve for what is inevitable.
verses.hi: क्योंकि पैदा हुएकी जरूर मृत्यु होगी और मरे हुएका जरूर जन्म होगा। इस (जन्म-मरण-रूप परिवर्तन के प्रवाह) का परिहार अर्थात् निवारण नहीं हो सकता। अतः इस विषयमें तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिये।
verses.short: Whoever's born will die, and whoever dies comes back. Don't stress over what can't be avoided.
verses.commentary: Birth is sure to happen to that which is dead death is sure to happen to what which is born. Birth and death are certainly unavoidable. Therefore, you should not grieve over an inevitable matter.

verses.en: O Arjuna, beings have an unknown beginning, a known middle, and an unknown end. What is there to grieve about in all this?
verses.hi: हे भारत ! सभी प्राणी जन्मसे पहले अप्रकट थे और मरनेके बाद अप्रकट हो जायँगे, केवल बीचमें ही प्रकट दीखते हैं। अतः इसमें शोक करनेकी बात ही क्या है?
verses.short: We come from the unknown and go back to it. We only see the middle part. Why panic?
verses.commentary: The physical body is a combination of the five elements. It is seen by the physical eyes only after the five elements have entered into such combination. After death, the body disintegrates and the five elements go back to their source it cannot be seen. Therefore, the body can be seen only in the middle state. The relationship as son, friend, teacher, father, mother, wife, brother and sister is formed through the body on account of attachment and Moha (delusion). Just as planks unite and separate in a river, just as pilgrims unite and separate in a public inn, so also fathers, mothers, sons and brothers unite and separate in this world. This world is a very big public inn. People unite and separate.There is no pot in the beginning and in the end. Even if you see the pot in the middle, you should think and feel that it is illusory and does not really exist. So also there is no body in the beginning and in the end. That which does not exist in the beginning and in the end must be illusory in the middle also. You must think and feel that the body does not really exist in the middle as well.He who thus understands the nature of the body and all human relationships based on it, will not grieve.

verses.en: One regards This (self) as a wonder; another speaks of It as a wonder; yet another hears of It as a wonder; and even after hearing of It, one does not know It.
verses.hi: कोई इस शरीरीको आश्चर्यकी तरह देखता है और वैसे ही अन्य कोई इसका आश्चर्यकी तरह वर्णन करता है तथा अन्य कोई इसको आश्चर्यकी तरह सुनता है; और इसको सुनकर भी कोई नहीं जानता। अर्थात यह शरीरी दुर्विज्ञेय है।
verses.short: Some see the soul as a miracle, some talk about it, some hear about it. Few actually get it.
verses.commentary: The verse may also be interpreted in this manner. He that sees, hears and speaks of the Self is a wonderful man. Such a man is very rare. He is one among many thousands. Thus the Self is very hard to understand.

verses.en: The self in the body, O Arjuna, is eternal and indestructible. This is the case for all selves in all bodies. Therefore, it is not fitting for you to feel grief for any being.
verses.hi: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन! सबके देहमें यह देही नित्य ही अवध्य है। इसलिये सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके लिये अर्थात् किसी भी प्राणीके लिये तुम्हें शोक नहीं करना चाहिये।
verses.short: The soul in every body is eternal. Nobody is ever truly lost. Don't drown in grief.
verses.commentary: The body of any creature may be destroyed but the Self cannot be killed. Therefore you should not grieve regarding any creature whatever, Bhishma or anybody else.

verses.en: Further, considering also your own duty, it does not befit you to waver. For, to a Kshatriya, there is no greater good than a righteous war.
verses.hi: अपने स्वधर्म (क्षात्रधर्म) को देखकर भी तुम्हें विकम्पित अर्थात् कर्तव्य-कर्मसे विचलित नहीं होना चाहिये; क्योंकि धर्ममय युद्धसे बढ़कर क्षत्रियके लिये दूसरा कोई कल्याणकारक कर्म नहीं है।
verses.short: This is literally your role. Backing out of the right fight doesn't suit you.
verses.commentary: Lord Krishna now gives to Arjuna wordly reasons for fighting. Up to this time, He talked to Arjuna on the immortality of the Self and gave him philosophical reasons. Now He says to Arjuna, O Arjuna Fighting is a Kshatriyas own duty. You ought not to swerve from that duty. To a Kshatriyta (one born in the warrior or ruling class) nothing is more welcome than a righteous war. A warrior should fight.

verses.en: Happy are the Ksatriyas, O Arjuna, to whom such a war comes of its own accord; it opens the gates to heaven.
verses.hi: अपने-आप प्राप्त हुआ युद्ध खुला हुआ स्वर्गका दरवाजा भी है। हे पृथानन्दन ! वे क्षत्रिय बड़े सुखी (भाग्यशाली) हैं, जिनको ऐसा युद्ध प्राप्त होता है।
verses.short: A real chance to stand up for what's right is rare. Lucky are those who get one.
verses.commentary: The scriptures declare that if a Kshatriya dies for a righteous cause on the battlefield, he at once goes to heaven.

verses.en: But if you do not fight this righteous war, you will be turning away from your duty and honor, and will incur sin.
verses.hi: अब अगर तू यह धर्ममय युद्ध नहीं करेगा,  तो अपने धर्म और कीर्तिका त्याग करके पापको प्राप्त होगा।
verses.short: Skip this fight and you lose your purpose, your respect, and your peace.
verses.commentary: The Lord reminds Arjuna of the fame he had already earned and which he would now lose if he refused to fight. Arjuna had acired great fame by fighting with Lord Siva. Arjuna proceeded on a pilgrimage to the Himalayas. He fought with Siva Who appeared in the guise of a mountaineer (Kirata) and got from Him the Pasupatastra, a celestial weapon.

verses.en: Further, people will speak ill of you for all time, and for one accustomed to being honored, dishonor is worse than death.
verses.hi: और सब प्राणी भी तेरी सदा रहनेवाली अपकीर्तिका कथन अर्थात निंदा करेंगे। वह अपकीर्ति सम्मानित मनुष्यके लिये मृत्युसे भी बढ़कर दुःखदायी होती है।
verses.short: Run away and people will talk about it forever. For someone respected, that hurts more than anything.
verses.commentary: The world also will ever recount thy infamy which will survive thee for a long time. Death is really preferable to disgrace to one who has been honoured as a great hero and mighty warrior with noble alities.

verses.en: The great warriors will think that you have fled from battle out of fear. Those who held you in high esteem will now speak of you disparagingly.
verses.hi: महारथीलोग तुझे भयके कारण युद्धसे उपरत (हटा) हुआ मानेंगे। जिनकी धारणामें तू बहुमान्य हो चुका है, उनकी दृष्टिमें तू लघुताको प्राप्त हो जायगा।
verses.short: The legends will think you got scared. The ones who hyped you up will lose respect.
verses.commentary: Duryodhana and others will certainly think that you have fled from the battle from fear of Karna and others, but not through compassion and reverence for elders and teachers. Duryodhana and others who have shown great esteem to you on account of your chivalry, bravery and other noble alities, will think very lightly of you and treat you with contempt.

verses.en: Your enemies, slandering your prowess, will use words that should never be uttered. What could be more painful than that?
verses.hi: तेरे शत्रुलोग तेरी सार्मथ्यकी निन्दा करते हुए न कहनेयोग्य बहुत-से वचन भी कहेंगे। उससे बढ़कर और दुःखकी बात क्या होगी?
verses.short: Haters will roast you nonstop. What's more painful than that?
verses.commentary: There is really no pain more unbearable and tormenting that that of slander thus incurred.

verses.en: If slain, you will win heaven; or if victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise, O Arjuna, resolved to fight.
verses.hi: अगर युद्धमें तू मारा जायगा तो तुझे स्वर्गकी प्राप्ति होगी और अगर युद्धमें तू जीत जायगा तो पृथ्वीका राज्य भोगेगा। अतः हे कुन्तीनन्दन! तू युद्धके लिये निश्चय करके खड़ा हो जा।
verses.short: Lose and you still win something. Win and you get it all. So get up and fight.
verses.commentary: In either case you will be benefited. Therefore, stand up with the firm resolution I will coner the enemy or die.

verses.en: Holding pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as equal, gird yourself up for the battle. Thus, you shall not incur any sin.
verses.hi: जय-पराजय, लाभ-हानि और सुख-दुःखको समान करके फिर युद्धमें लग जा। इस प्रकार युद्ध करनेसे तू पापको प्राप्त नहीं होगा।
verses.short: Pleasure or pain, gain or loss, win or fail: treat them the same and just do your duty.
verses.commentary: This is the Yoga of eanimity or the doctrine of poise in action. If anyone does any action with the above mental attitude or balanced state of mind he will not reap the fruits of his action. Such an action will lead to the purification of his heart and freedom from birth and death. One has to develop such a balanced state of mind through continous struggle and vigilant efforts.

verses.en: This Buddhi concerning the Self (Sankhya) has been imparted to you. Now listen to this with regard to Yoga, by following which you will get rid of the bondage of Karma.
verses.hi: हे पार्थ! यह समबुद्धि तेरे लिए पहले सांख्ययोगमें कही गयी, अब तू इसको कर्मयोगके विषयमें सुन; जिस समबुद्धिसे युक्त हुआ तू कर्मबन्धनका त्याग कर देगा।
verses.short: Theory done. Now the practical: how to work without getting trapped by your actions.
verses.commentary: Lord Krishna taught Jnana (knowledge) to Arjuna till now. (Sankhya Yoga is the path of Vedanta or Jnana Yoga, which treats of the nature of the Atman or the Self and the methods to attain Selfrealisation. It is not the Sankhya philosophy of sage Kapila.) He is now giving to teach Arjuna the technie or secret of Karma Yoga endowed with which he (or anybody else) can break through the bonds of Karma. The Karma Yogi should perform work without expectation of fruits of his actions, without the idea of agency (or the notin I do this), without attachment, after annihilating or going beyond all the pairs of opposites such as heat and cold, gain and loss, victoyr and defeat, etc. Dharma and Adharma, or merit and demerit will not touch that Karma Yogi who works without attachment and egoism. The Karma Yogi consecrates all his works and their fruits as offerings unto the Lord (Isvararpanam) and thus obtains the grace of the Lord (Isvaraprasada).

verses.en: Here, there is no loss of effort, nor any accrual of evil. Even a little of this Dharma (called Karma Yoga) protects one from the great fear.
verses.hi: मनुष्यलोकमें इस समबुद्धिरूप धर्मके आरम्भका नाश नहीं होता, इसके अनुष्ठानका उलटा फल भी नहीं होता और इसका थोड़ासा भी अनुष्ठान (जन्म-मरणरूप) महान् भयसे रक्षा कर लेता है।
verses.short: On this path no effort is ever wasted. Even a little practice protects you from big fears.
verses.commentary: If a religious ceremony is left uncompleted, it is a wastage as the performer cannot realise the fruits. But it is not so in the case of Karma Yoga because every action causes immediate purification of the heart.In agriculture there is uncertainty. The farmer may till the land, plough and sow the seed but he may not get a crop if there is no rain. This is not so in Karma Yoga. There is no uncertainty at all.
